subject: Request for credit calculation clarification — GreenStone production latency windows
messages:
From: GreenStone Payments <ops@greenstonepay.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spikes + missing credits for 11/27

Rachel —

We reviewed our monthly invoice and uptime report and it shows no credit for the 11/27 production latency spike between 01:10–01:35 UTC. Our customers saw request failures and elevated p99s. Can you confirm Redwood's calculation? The window overlaps with a scheduled maintenance note we received, but we were told that maintenance pages were limited to 01:00–01:15 UTC. We need a breakdown (total downtime minutes attributed to Redwood vs third-party log ingestion) and whether GreenStone is eligible for an SLA credit.

Attaching our internal incident timeline.

— Jamie Park
Operations, GreenStone Payments
attachments: GS_incident_timeline_1127.pdf (pdf)
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: GreenStone Payments <ops@greenstonepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes + missing credits for 11/27

Jamie —

Thanks for flagging this. I’m pulling the detailed SLO/uptime math now and looping in our infra lead (Dev) and SLA owner (Marissa). At first glance the dates/times on our side show a partial degradation from 01:07–01:38 UTC. A couple of clarifying notes so we don't talk past each other:

- Our policy excludes customer-visible impact caused solely by a third-party provider (see SLA section 3.2).
- We also prorate credits for partial degradations; we will provide an itemized minute-level apportionment.

I’ll come back with the minute-by-minute attribution and the calculation file.

– Rachel Kim
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: GreenStone — request for credit breakdown (incident attached)

FYI — GreenStone is asking why they didn’t get credit for the 01:10–01:35 UTC window. They received a maintenance notice for 01:00–01:15 UTC; logs indicate our partial degradation extended beyond that.

Key asks:
- Can Dev confirm whether the extra 20+ minutes are attributable to our backend or to LogFlow (their logging/metrics provider)?
- If LogFlow caused the majority of the extended p99s, we need to document their outage to determine exclusion.

I attached the GreenStone timeline to this thread and will drop our calculation file once Dev sends the raw minute-level status.

— Rachel
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: GreenStone — request for credit breakdown (incident attached)

Quick technical summary (raw):

- Our ingress frontend reported elevated queue depth and 5xx spike starting at 01:07 UTC; internal routing layer recovered to baseline at 01:36 UTC.
- During 01:12–01:30 UTC we saw a surge of delayed acknowledgements from our async logger (LogFlow) causing backpressure on the write path.
- We pulled a full trace bundle and a minute-level availability vector and uploaded it to the shared drive (support_log_20261128.zip). The trace shows ~14 minutes of clear Redwood-side latency impact where requests were delayed >500ms and ~9 minutes dominated by LogFlow timeouts.

Conclusion: this is a mixed cause — both a short maintenance window and a downstream logging provider overload. I recommend apportioning the 29 minutes as: Redwood responsibility 14 mins, LogFlow exclusion 9 mins, scheduled maintenance overlap 6 mins (per our maintenance notice).

I'll attach the minute-by-minute CSV to SLA_uptime_calc_notes.xlsx for Marissa to run the credit formula.

— Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: support@logflow.io
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident 1127 — acknowledgement and incident summary

Marissa / team —

We confirm LogFlow experienced a degraded ingestion cluster between 01:10–01:28 UTC due to a replication lag in our EU ingest shard after a routing rebalancing job. We have an internal postmortem and have assigned LogFlow-INC-673. We recognize this may be an exclude under Redwood's SLA too; we will share our incident report and timeline (attaching: logflow_postmortem_1128.pdf).

Apologies for the downstream impact — we are open to coordinating evidence for GreenStone's request.

— Claire Tan
Support Lead, LogFlow Inc.
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: GreenStone Payments <ops@greenstonepay.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, support@logflow.io
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Resolution: GreenStone SLA credit apportionment for 2026-11-27 incident

Jamie —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary of our findings and the credit calculation:

- Total customer-observed impact window: 01:07–01:38 UTC (31 minutes).
- Apportioned minutes: Redwood responsibility = 14 minutes; Scheduled maintenance (Redwood notice) = 6 minutes; Third-party (LogFlow) = 11 minutes.
- Applying the SLA credit formula (section 4.1) to the 14 Redwood minutes results in a 7% service credit on the November invoice for the GreenStone account. We are issuing that credit programmatically — you will see REFUND-GS-202611 in your billing portal within 3–5 business days.

Notes and evidence: we attached the minute-by-minute calculation (SLA_uptime_calc_notes.xlsx) and LogFlow's postmortem. Per our policy we exclude the 11 minutes attributed solely to LogFlow. If GreenStone would like broader leniency beyond the contractual calculation, we can discuss a one-time goodwill credit — let me know.

Thanks to Dev and the LogFlow team for quick evidence sharing.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
SLA & Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_uptime_calc_notes.xlsx (spreadsheet), logflow_postmortem_1128.pdf (pdf)
